classification.classification_note: The saved crash is a stack-use-after-return read. `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` copies a font-backed `Coverage` object into constructor-local stack variable `t1`; `CoverageFormat2::Iter::init` then stores a pointer into that local copy, and `iter.more()` later dereferences it after the constructor has returned.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470094 (harfbuzz): Stack-use-after-return READ 1 found by fuzz target hb-subset-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470094
bug_description.normalized: The staged 284427-byte witness `poc` is accepted as a font face, and the crashing `trySubset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)` iteration enters GSUB substitution closure while `hb_subset_plan_create()` computes glyph closure. In `SingleSubstFormat2::closure()`, HarfBuzz resolves the subtable's `coverage` offset and constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter> iter (this+coverage)`. Vulnerable `hb_auto_t` takes that `Coverage` by value as local `t1` and calls `Type::init(t1)`. On the observed format-2 path, `CoverageFormat2::Iter::init(const CoverageFormat2 &c_)` then stores `c = &c_`, so the iterator points into the constructor-local copy `t1.u.format2`. After the constructor returns, the first loop condition `iter.more()` reuses that dangling pointer to read `c->rangeRecord.len`, and AddressSanitizer reports a stack-use-after-return READ of size 1 in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const` at `src/hb-machinery.hh:625`. The patch fixes this by replacing the generic by-value `hb_auto_t(T1 t1)` constructor with pointer/reference overloads so `Coverage` objects are no longer copied accidentally.

source.description: First vulnerability-relevant project read of attacker-controlled font data on the crashing path. This loop initializer resolves the current GSUB subtable's `coverage` offset against the input font and materializes the `Coverage` object that seeds the iterator state.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is the saved 284427-byte font blob `poc` (sha256 `15bb0c9e266e6e722d4715111aff56578dc2ea5ad68e639c34f8c8b02342f2b2`). On the crashing `drop_ot_layout=false` subset iteration, this statement resolves the font's `coverage` table for a `SingleSubstFormat2` subtable; the saved stack through `CoverageFormat2::Iter::more()` shows that the observed `Coverage` union is in format 2.

sink.description: ASan sink. Converting the stale `rangeRecord.len` field to `unsigned short` reads the two bytes of the dead `BEInt` object inside constructor-local `t1`, producing the reported stack-use-after-return read.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` here and says the accessed address is inside local variable `t1` in frame `hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage::Iter>::hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage>` at `src/hb-dsalgs.hh:495`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The generic `hb_auto_t` constructor takes the font-backed `Coverage` by value, creating constructor-local stack copy `t1` instead of preserving the caller's reference. The iterator initialization then aliases that ephemeral copy.
root_cause.note: The fix patch changes this constructor family to pointer/reference overloads only, with an explicit comment that the old template caused accidental copies and related bugs.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete attacker-shaped state relevant to the bug is the `Coverage` object resolved from the font's `coverage` offset for the current `SingleSubstFormat2` subtable. That object is what step 2 copies into stack local `t1`.

parser_admitted.description: The crash only occurs in the `trySubset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)` arm. There `close_over_gsub` is true, so subset planning enters GSUB closure and reaches the `SingleSubstFormat2::closure()` loop that constructs the buggy iterator.

coarse_trace.summary: One `trySubset` iteration runs with `drop_ot_layout=false`, so `hb_subset()` builds a subset plan that closes over GSUB substitutions for the attacker-controlled font.
Subset planning dispatches GSUB lookups and reaches a `SingleSubstFormat2` subtable whose `coverage` field is resolved from the input font.
The closure loop constructs `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` from that font-backed `Coverage`, but the generic `hb_auto_t(T1 t1)` constructor copies it by value into stack local `t1`.

coarse_trace.function: OT::CoverageFormat2::Iter::init / OT::CoverageFormat2::Iter::more / BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const
coarse_trace.summary: The format-2 iterator stores a pointer into the constructor-local copy, the constructor returns, and the first `iter.more()` reuses that dangling pointer to read `rangeRecord.len`, producing the recorded stack-use-after-return.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing GSUB-closure path, this loop initializer resolves the current subtable's `coverage` offset against the attacker-controlled font and passes that font-backed `Coverage` object into `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>`. The observed stack through `CoverageFormat2::Iter::more()` shows the witnessed `Coverage` is format 2.

Root cause. The generic constructor copies the font-backed `Coverage` from step 1 by value into constructor-local stack variable `t1` and then initializes the iterator from that copy. The patch removes this by-value path and keeps only pointer/reference overloads.

On the observed format-2 arm, iterator initialization stores `c = &c_`. Here `c_` is the `CoverageFormat2` subobject inside constructor-local copy `t1`, so the iterator's internal pointer now aliases stack storage owned by step 2 rather than the original font-backed object.

fine_trace.code: inline bool more (void) { return i < c->rangeRecord.len; }
fine_trace.note: After the `hb_auto_t` constructor in step 2 returns, the local copy `t1` is dead but `iter.c` from step 3 still points into it. The first loop-condition check therefore dereferences the stale pointer to fetch `rangeRecord.len` from out-of-lifetime stack storage.

Sink. Evaluating step 4's `c->rangeRecord.len` converts the stale `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>` object to `unsigned short`, so this operator reads the bytes of the dead `t1` copy. ASan reports the stack-use-after-return here and identifies the poisoned stack object as local `t1` from step 2.

trySubset(hb_face_t*, unsigned int const*, int, bool, bool)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASan's frame-object dump says the invalid address is inside local `t1` in `hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage::Iter>::hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage>` at `src/hb-dsalgs.hh:495`, which is exactly the fine-trace root cause where the font-backed `Coverage` is copied by value.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch replaces `template <typename T1> hb_auto_t (T1 t1)` with pointer/reference overloads, preventing the accidental by-value `Coverage` copy that created stack local `t1`.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `stack-use-after-return` at `src/hb-machinery.hh:625` and explicitly says the accessed bytes are inside object `t1` in frame `hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage::Iter>::hb_auto_t<OT::Coverage>` at `src/hb-dsalgs.hh:495`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_42470094-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'` and reproduced the AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const`.

format.name: OpenType/TrueType font blob
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 284427-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `15bb0c9e266e6e722d4715111aff56578dc2ea5ad68e639c34f8c8b02342f2b2`) as consumed by the saved ARVO run. That font must remain accepted by `hb_face_create` and, on the crashing `trySubset(..., drop_ot_layout=false)` iteration, must preserve the observed path where GSUB closure reaches `SingleSubstFormat2::closure()` on a subtable whose `coverage` resolves to a format-2 `Coverage` object. The witness must keep the same bug trigger: `hb_auto_t<Coverage::Iter>` copies that `Coverage` by value into constructor-local `t1`, `CoverageFormat2::Iter::init` stores `c = &c_` into that copy, and the subsequent `iter.more()` dereferences `c` after the constructor returns. This contract is limited to that witnessed font and closure path; it does not generalize to other font layouts or GSUB tables.
